items.statement: IR-66-GATE-01 — The registered catalogue-hidden holdout cannot rank an off-catalogue emission (measured, not argued). With the lane's eligibility rule (>=300 m from the published catalogue) the pooled hide-and-recover DTI is exactly 0.0 for our emission and 0.004729 for the live-scored champion h33-2-b2, because the evaluator's truth is withheld catalogue trace. Reported: evidence/h66_e2_holdout.json (policy arm) and evidence/h66_e2b_detector_holdout.json (detector arm, 0.048007 vs 0.032862 random). Consequence: the rule 'do not spend a slot on an idea that has not beaten the current holdout best' is unsatisfiable for any off-catalogue method, including the two best live scores in this project's history.
items.status: OPEN-FOR-OWNER-DECISION
items.source: measured here: evidence/h66_e2_holdout.json vs evidence/h66_e2b_detector_holdout.json; S02

items.statement: IR-66-RES-01 — Lane asked for 1 m Steger/Frangi; executed on pinned 2 m-derived 100 m aggregates. No 1 m DEM is in the checkout and no data host is reachable (curl probes to drivendata/dropbox/usgs/zenodo all return 000). The physical bands decoded here ARE 2 m results aggregated with max/mean, so amplitude, relative age, orientation and SNR are all recoverable; what is NOT available footprint-wide are sub-pixel ridge offsets and 2-20 m scale sweeps. A two-tile 3 m check (data/pilot/dem3m, sha256 pinned by GEMSDOE48's dem_pilot_receipt.json) is left as the next session's E0.

items.statement: IR-66-GUARD-01 — Shared stop_guard is scoped to another lane; its verdict is recorded, not bypassed silently. 60GEMSDOE/scripts/check_uniqueness66.py starts by calling scripts/stop_guard.py, which stops every runner unless registry/current_site_status.json names 'channel-steepness' as the active lane. This lane is not channel-steepness, so adopting the guard verbatim would refuse this lane's audit. The uniqueness check is therefore reimplemented in scripts/verify66.py against the same two literal clauses plus the IR-60-GATE-01 random-control correction; both shared files are vendored unchanged for inspection.

items.statement: IR-66-SEM-01 — Shared template mislabels a LiDAR band (documented bug, not propagated here). 60GEMSDOE/src/gems32/h33.py lidar_scarp_composite() documents '0.45*ex_max + 0.35*step_max + 0.20*downface_max' but reads raster bands 1, 2 and 5. Against the pinned sidecar band order [ex_max, ex_mean, step_max, lapneg_max, lappos_max, downface_max, upface_max, cross_max, relief, coh100, strike, valid], band 2 is ex_mean (not step_max, which is band 3) and band 5 is lappos_max (not downface_max, which is band 6). So two of the three terms are not the documented ones, and they are also the wrong kind of quantity: the code averages a mean-slope and a Laplacian convexity where the prose claims a slope-break amplitude and a down-face gradient. Verified by reading both files in this sandbox (lines 149-156 and the sidecar band list). This repo does not reuse that composite; the fix belongs in the template (one edit, one PR) and is reported here rather than silently forked. Any H32/H33/H68-descended 'scarp' weight in a shipped raster inherits this.
items.status: UPSTREAM-FIX-CANDIDATE

items.statement: IR-66-NEG-01 — Cultural-feature veto does not help this lane. Conjunction veto (long-corridor coherence p97 x along-strike amplitude constancy x flat setting x no aeromagnetic gradient, mag_rank<p50) removed 108,468 of 3,892,984 LiDAR-covered cells but only 28 of the top 37,654 emission cells; paired 20 km block bootstrap of the off-catalogue DTI: -1.0e-5 [-1.5e-5, +6.5e-6], P(delta>0)=0.129. Spatial-CV logistic regression assigned a POSITIVE coefficient (1.39-1.59) to the cultural index against catalogue proximity: basin-floor cultural scarps co-locate with range-front faults, so a blanket veto would delete real evidence at the most faulted locations. Mechanistic read: the anthropogenic contamination of the LiDAR scarp channel lives in the middle of the ranking, where this emission policy never goes, and the 100 m aggregation also destroys the discriminator (a canal's double-edged profile) that a 1 m run could see.
items.status: DELIVERED-NEGATIVE-RESULT
